## CVE-2026-123218: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability

Source-reported by [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-123218).

CVE-2026-123218 (official CVSS 9.8): IBM Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 through 5.0.19 could allow an authorized user to craft a specific message to bypass user authorization and gain full administrative privileges. CISA lists it as exploited in the wild.

Defensive action: Apply the fix in the vendor's advisory (https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/7295921); the CVE record lists as affected: Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 through 5.0.19. If no update or mitigation is available, take the product out of service.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Added to the CISA KEV catalog 9 Nov 2026; first seen by SecOpsAI 10 Nov 2026, 00:20 UTC.

Identifiers and scores checked automatically against cve.org and NVD.

| Claim | Check | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CVE-2026-123218 exists | confirmed | [cve.org](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-123218) |
| CVSS 9.8 | confirmed | [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123218) |
| exploited in the wild | confirmed | [CISA KEV](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-123218) |

## CVE-2026-123158: OpenBSD OpenSSH Unexpected Status Code or Return Value Vulnerability

Source-reported by [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?search_api_fulltext=CVE-2026-123158).

CVE-2026-123158 (official CVSS 8.1): sshd in OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on Linux, when musl libc is used without PAM, lacks a workaround for a password authentication bypass (related to misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash). For some configurations of accounts, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds. CISA lists it as exploited in the wild.

Defensive action: Apply the vendor's security update; the CVE record lists the fix in 10.6p2. If no update or mitigation is available, take the product out of service.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Added to the CISA KEV catalog 9 Nov 2026; first seen by SecOpsAI 10 Nov 2026, 00:20 UTC.

## node-opcua: Namespace-Level RBAC Fail-Open - Anonymous Write/Call Bypass via Unbound `DefaultRolePermissions

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xggf-m53x-jc3f).

CVE-2026-95860 (official CVSS 9.1): Servers with no declared policy, nodes with explicit per-node permissions, and correctly bound programmatic namespace metadata are outside the authorization-bypass case. This issue is fixed in version 2.180.0.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: node-opcua 2.180.0, node-opcua-address-space 2.180.0, node-opcua-server 2.180.0.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

## Kubeflow Pipelines: Reflected XSS in the frontend pod information and events error responses

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3qx-frcg-j979).

CVE-2026-88986 (official CVSS 6.1): An unauthenticated attacker can craft a link that executes JavaScript in the frontend origin when a user who satisfies the deployment's authentication and route-access requirements follows it and reaches an affected response. Cookie disclosure depends on cookie attributes, and server-side code execution or availability impact is not established.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/kubeflow/pipelines 0.0.0-20251010122814-fedc25e3f725.

## GPUStack: Authentication bypass via trusted loopback source (reverse-proxy TCP peer or X-GPUStack-Real-IP header) grants unauthenticated admin

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr).

CVE-2026-102895 (official CVSS 9.8): The bypass allowed unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. Exploitation was observed in the wild against a 2.1.1 deployment.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: gpustack 2.2.0.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue. Exploitation is reported but not confirmed by CISA KEV.

## Kubeflow Pipelines API server lacks authorization for shared pipeline uploads

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rjr3-43j3-4q8g).

CVE-2026-77596 (official CVSS 9.6): A low-privilege tenant can create shared pipelines or inject attacker-controlled versions into existing shared pipelines without the required write permission; if the API server is directly reachable without an authenticating proxy, an unauthenticated caller can exploit the same bypass, while deployments protected by such a proxy do not expose anonymous access.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/kubeflow/pipelines 0.0.0-20260909234119-62516d8c525f.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

Published 9 Nov 2026, 22:22 UTC; first seen by SecOpsAI 9 Nov 2026, 23:23 UTC.

## Kubeflow Pipelines: RBAC bypass on shared pipelines allows any authenticated user to delete or modify global pipelines

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ghgh-57qv-h687).

CVE-2026-88984 (official CVSS 7.2): Read-only access to shared pipelines remains intentional, single-user deployments intentionally bypass multi-user checks, and execution of a modified pipeline is a conditional downstream consequence. The separate shared-pipeline multipart upload authorization path is outside this advisory and is not remediated by version 2.16.1.

Defensive action: Upgrade to a fixed release: github.com/kubeflow/pipelines 0.0.0-20260420170029-186dd1f3b040.

Limitations: Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.
